reviews.comment: Be prepared to catch 20 bugs and spend a lot of time outside trying to do the homework for this class, but he is a very nice guy. The exams are very difficult to get an A on but easy to pass if you study.

Dr. Behmer is great!!! You can tell he really cares about his students, and will recognize you and remember your name. In this class, you had to take 20 iNat photos, 5 good photos, 4 exams, 2 lab practicals and a semester long insect collection. This is probably the hardest 200 level course I've ever taken but the teacher made it worth it!
If you don't have a religion, get one and pray.

Dr. Behmer's lectures were so engaging and really prepared me for the exams. You also get a cheat sheet. There is occasional extra credit for going to class. He genuinely cares about his students' success and is accessible outside of class if you need help understanding the material. He also shares music recommendations that are very good.

Dr. Behmer was a professor that did his job well, but nothing extraordinary. His interest in insects made the class more interesting. The tests can be a little hard from what I thought would be an easy class, but the extra credit helps. He would go on Twitter in the middle of the class and show us really cool insects which made the class fun.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Behmer is great! He is super passionate about what he teaches, which really helps the class stay engaged. he's tough, but actively helps you learn what to expect and how to take his tests. I loved his class!

Pretty good professor. I've seen a lot of negative reviews that seem to have a similar writing style and are likely from one person on multiple accounts. Dr. Behmer's exams are easy if you just memorize the color coded parts of the lecture slides. He also gives lots of extra credit just for showing up to class.

I did not enjoy this class. He is a nice man, but I did not like his teaching style at all. I would not recommend him to other people. I have friends that took the same class with a different professor that received an A. This is a 201 class; it should not be this difficult. Do not take this class.

Great class. I'm not sure what all the negative reviews are about (kind of suspicious most were posted on the same day). It's not necessarily an easy A, but lectures are engaging and Dr. Behmer is passionate about the topic. Heavy on taxonomy and you will have to memorize orders. Treat it like a bio class, make flashcards, and you will be fine.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Some of the reviews here are really dramatic. Behmer grades incredibly leniently. His exams are difficult and he doesnt have many assignments, but hes incredibly kind, helpful and knowledgeable. His lectures are great & really thought out. Even though his class is tough, I learned so much and would be glad to take it again.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The other reviews speak for themselves. From the first exam to the fourth, almost a third of the class Q-dropped this class for a reason. The class shouldn't be hard, it's literally 201, but Behmer makes it difficult for no reason at all. His exams were consistently failing grades and he offered no curve. You can't prepare for these exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: In class, we would go over the lectures and he would facilitate a discussion-style learning environment. This really helped with creating long-term memory with active recall in class. His quizzes and tests are hard, but you do get a cheat sheet. My tip to you is to go to class, take notes, and know that you will have to work hard to succeed!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took Ento 201 because everyone told me it was a fun class and somewhat of an easy A. However, with Behmer, I am failing. There is zero homework, so your entire grade depends on his very open-ended exams. He gives you an idea on what to study and then throws in questions that make no sense because they were not a part of what you should study.

I have talked to other students in ENTO201 that have other profs that say this class is a breeze. The first 2 exam averages have been Ds or worse, and he does not make them any easier. He must think we are the issue, but that is not the case. Lectures are boring, and unless you are absolutely dying to learn about bugs, take another prof or class.

Dr. Behmer is a great prof, loves insects and what he teaches, and he likes to show neat videos and geek out over his favorite bugs, namely grasshoppers. When attendance is sparse he gives out bonus points, and gave extra credit on an exam we had on Halloween if we dressed in an ento costume. Detailed tests, but lab is easy and boosts your grade

I came in with a ton of experience in Entomology as far as classification.  His lectures are interesting but are long and tend to get old toward the end of the semester. Take notes on what he actually says in class because that is what will be on his test.  No homework, just study every little thing for tests.

Behmer is awesome, he tells lots of cool side stories and facts about the insects covered in the course. The lab is really fun because you make your own insect collection through the semester and submit it as your final project for lab,there are no study guides for exams but they are directly off lectures and the short chapters assignment, easy A

He gave extra credit now and then for just showing up. A test question on the test was, what insect was featured in a south park episode (which we saw in class). Unfortunately there is no review for this class so you have to be able to study on your own terms, but he is more than willing to help if you don't understand. The lab however, is meh.
He is really nice and helpful and his supplementary materials are great!  His labs are easy and worth a lot of points.
